title: HSK2 Gate 10 · Eastern Jin
explanationEn: Gate 10: Eastern Jin. Read the words below, then read the story out loud. The story is the same one you read on the map — this is the start of it.
explanation: 第10关：东晋。先读下面的词，再大声读短文。这段短文就是地图上那个故事的开头。
passage: 一千六百多年以前，晋朝有一位很有名的诗人，叫陶渊明。他年轻的时候做过官。做官可以有钱，也可以有名。可是他一点也不喜欢那样的日子。
passageEn: More than sixteen hundred years ago, in the Jin dynasty, there was a famous poet called Tao Yuanming. When he was young he served as an official. An official could have money, and could have a name. But he did not like that life at all.

comprehension.questionEn: Read the first sentence again. What does it tell you?
comprehension.question: 再读第一句。它说了什么？
comprehension.answerEn: More than sixteen hundred years ago, in the Jin dynasty, there was a famous poet called Tao Yuanming.
comprehension.answer: 一千六百多年以前，晋朝有一位很有名的诗人，叫陶渊明。

comprehension.questionEn: Read the third sentence again. Who or what is it about?
comprehension.question: 再读第三句。它说的是谁，或者是什么？
comprehension.answerEn: An official could have money, and could have a name.
comprehension.answer: 做官可以有钱，也可以有名。

comprehension.questionEn: Read the whole passage out loud, then say one sentence from memory.
comprehension.question: 大声读一遍短文，再试着背出其中的一句。
comprehension.answerEn: Any one sentence from the passage above.
comprehension.answer: 上面短文里的任何一句。

check.promptEn: In the story, what does 一 mean?
check.prompt: 短文里的“一”是什么意思？
check.explanationEn: 一 (yī) means "one" — you can find it in the passage above.
check.explanation: “一”（yī）的意思是“one”，就在上面的短文里。

check.promptEn: In the story, what does 千 mean?
check.prompt: 短文里的“千”是什么意思？
check.explanationEn: 千 (qiān) means "thousand" — you can find it in the passage above.
check.explanation: “千”（qiān）的意思是“thousand”，就在上面的短文里。

options.text: More than sixteen hundred years ago, in the Jin dynasty, there was a famous poet called Tao Yuanming.
Long, long ago, it rained in China for many days, and a great flood came.
The flood went into the fields, and into many people's homes.
People had nowhere to live, and could only go up the mountains to live.
